_about: How big a party is (rule 75b: 'a party is sized by Battle Brothers' math, never twelve against twelve, and the first roads give a few thugs'). The INPUTS and their directions are Battle Brothers' (the wiki's Game Mechanics page and GROK_60): roster strength, the job's skulls, days, distance from towns, the combat difficulty, the count words. The wiki gives NO arithmetic from those to a head count, and no unit costs, so the few coefficients that make a number are OURS, draft, each marked 'ours', calibrated on the rule's own anchor (a fresh three-man crew's first job on day one is a few thugs) and waiting on Grok ask 22 (the hidden formulas) and TUNING. The MAKE-UP of a party (thugs, raiders, a leader) is COMBAT's, by tier, in ours.json enemy_tiers; this file only says how many.

roster_strength.quote: the strength of your roster (which equals a sum of individual strengths [10 + 2*(lvl-1)] of 12 strongest brothers) / (GROK_60) Peasant militia and manhunters use 14

count_words.quote: A few 2-3 / Some 4-6 / Many 7-10 / Lots 11-13 / A plethora 14+

day_cap.quote: A roaming party uses days and the crew score. Day scaling for those stops at day 100.

difficulty_by_pick.quote: Combat difficulty which is set at the start of the game, which increases both numbers and tier / COMBAT's scale (ours.json enemy_tiers): 0 Beginner, 1 Veteran, 2 Expert, 3 Legendary; each above Veteran counts as 20 days later

difficulty_count_mult.source: ours (draft, rule 75b): the direction is the wiki's ('increases both numbers and tier'), the size of the step is ours until Grok ask 22
difficulty_count_mult.quote: On higher combat difficulty harder enemy groups appear sooner.

job.source: ours (draft): a job 'scales with the strength of your roster, the skulls, and the type' (reference/library/grok/wiki/PAGES_ALL.tar.gz bb_all/0828_Game Mechanics.txt:105); one enemy per 10 points of roster strength (one level-1 man) at two skulls, calibrated so a fresh three-man crew's one-skull job is a few (rule 75b's anchor)
job.quote: Contract difficulty scales with the strength of your roster, the difficulty rating (skulls), the type of contract

roaming.source: ours (draft): roaming parties 'scale mostly with distance to civilization and time... also slightly with player strength, but less so than contracts' (reference/library/grok/wiki/PAGES_ALL.tar.gz bb_all/0828_Game Mechanics.txt:107); two on day one at a town's edge (rule 75b), about lots by day 100
roaming.quote: Difficulty of non-contract locations and roaming parties scales mostly with distance to civilization and time. Roaming parties also scale slightly with player strength, but less so than contracts
